plan.about: The audit plan the F1 Finance Audit Machine follows for the cash audit of the invented HANGS Construction Services LLC at June 30, 2026. The runner reads its thresholds from here; the Cash Audit Files system shows it. Every name and figure is invented.
plan.period: Fiscal year ended June 30, 2026; cash at June 30, 2026
plan.reader: The shareholders, the bonding company and Cinderbrook Bank read the year-end statements.

materiality.why: The same materiality serves every FY2026 audit area: 0.5% of the year's revenue, rounded down to the nearest ten thousand dollars. Anything under the clearly trivial amount is listed but not added up.

cash.insuredWhy: The FDIC insures deposits up to $250,000 per depositor at one bank; the rest is a concentration of credit risk the notes usually disclose.

assertions.how: Each balance confirmed by the bank directly to the audit team, and agreed to the June statement
The bank lists every account and loan; every ledger cash line is on a statement or a reconciliation
Both reconciliations recomputed; every reconciling item traced to the cutoff statement or the bank's written answer
Wires, transfers and receipts either side of June 30 tested against the bank's own records
Holds, liens, pledges, set-off and compensating balances asked of the bank; the loans confirmed
Restricted cash and uninsured balances against what the statements say

procedures.what: Tie cash across the trial balance, the ledger, the statements and the company's reconciliations, and propose materiality.
Check the confirmation chain and compare what the bank confirmed with the books.
Agree the confirmation to the June statements, match every June payment and recompute both reconciliations.
Trace every outstanding item to the July cutoff statement, age the old one, search the books for the bank's charges and explain the confirmation difference.
Test wires, transfers and receipts either side of June 30 and look for restricted cash, what the loans require and what must be disclosed.
Set what was found against materiality and write the workpapers and the draft memo. The CPA concludes.
